title: A Great White Shark Goes Through 30,000 Teeth

scenes.text: A great white shark goes through about thirty thousand teeth.
Its mouth shows around fifty teeth, with five or six more rows waiting behind them.
When a front tooth breaks or wears out, the next one moves forward like a conveyor belt.
That works because shark teeth sit in the gum, not in bone.
So a shark never has to stop hunting to repair its bite.
Thirty thousand teeth, and always a fresh row waiting.

description:
A great white shark goes through about 30,000 teeth in its lifetime.
New teeth move forward from rows behind, because the teeth sit in the gum rather than the bone.
How many teeth do you think you'd keep if you were a shark?
first_comment: Humans get two sets of teeth. Sharks get thousands. Which would you pick?
